To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) QFTs are UV finite if they can be viewed as low energy effective theories; and (2) the renormalization procedure is not needed in the new approach and it is in fact a part of the procedure of defining the ambiguities of the effective theories (i.e. the choice of the low energy renormalization conditions).
the finiteness and effectiveness of quantum field theory can be derived from a well defined underlying theory.
the QFTs are UV finite if they arise as the low energy and/or effective theories of some fundamental underlying theory (or theories).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following two issues: 1) the finiteness and the renormalization of the low energy and the effective theories; 2) the relation of these effective theories with the underlying ones and the implication for the canonical quantizaton procedure.
a new approach to the renormalization program and quantum field theory (QFT).
the finiteness problem of QFTs, the underlying theories of the low energy and the effective ones, and the canonical quantization problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new approach is a new attempt to make QFTs finite and well-defined.
QFTs are well-defined, complete and effective theories in the sense of the modern standard point view.
our approach is much simpler and more natural than any known renormalizationschemes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
QFTs (as effective theories) are well-defined, complete and UV finite in all respects, which is the most natural and simplest way to understand the finiteness of QFTs.

the UV finiteness is a general feature for all QFTs (in all space-time dimensions) as long as they can be considered as the low energy and/or effective theories of some fundamental underlying theory(s).
the finiteness of the QFTs can indeed be achieved in a natural way if we take the modern standard view seriously.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UV finiteness of QFT is not a problem at all if the QFT is considered as the effective one and the underlying theory is assumed to be complete and well-defined.
QFTs are in fact effective and finite theories.
the finiteness and the effectiveness of QFTs are not mutually exclusive.
